report.summary: Chunk 10 of 11: implements run execution, run ID generation, dry_run_plan, load_history, and append_history.
risks: dry_run_plan | medium | Sample string 'PLAN0000' used for prompt size estimation; may not reflect actual probe content. | Review if probe.build() can accept arbitrary sample or if actual probe content differs significantly.

load_history | medium | Uses json.loads with errors='replace' for file reading; may silently corrupt non-UTF-8 content. | Confirm that error handling for JSON parsing is sufficient; consider logging dropped lines.

claims.text: Prompt sizes are computed by BUILDING a sample body, so the plan reports the real payload rather than a guess about it.
claims.why: The code uses p.build(sample) where sample is 'PLAN0000' to compute prompt_chars.

claims.text: A plan that shows the payload but not the bill is how ``--live`` becomes a surprise. Naming a seat reads only its identity properties, which are pure.
claims.why: The claim about 'bill' and 'seat' properties refers to behavior not defined in this chunk; live_egress_lanes is called but its implementation is unseen.

claims.text: What WOULD be asked, of whom. Calls nothing -- no ``lane.ask`` is touched.
claims.why: The function only reads properties (vendor, model, endpoint, local) and calls probe.build() but does not invoke any method named 'ask'.

claims.text: A half-written last line (the machine was rebooted mid-append) must not take the health check down -- a canary that crashes on its own log is worse than no canary. Corrupt and foreign-schema lines are dropped silently and the rest of the file is still used.
claims.why: The code catches exceptions from json.loads, skips non-dict records, checks schema version, and checks status; it does not raise on corrupt lines.
The code does p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) and opens file with mode 'a' (append), never truncating.

claims.text: Append one record per probe result.
claims.why: The code iterates over run.results and creates one JSON line per result via r.to_record.

observations.what: dry_run_plan uses hardcoded sample string 'PLAN0000'; may not be representative of actual probe input.
load_history reads file with errors='replace', which may silently replace non-UTF-8 bytes; could mask encoding issues.
append_history writes lines joined with newline and adds trailing newline; if lines list is empty, returns 0 without writing anything.
run execution creates threads with daemon=True; join with timeout; if deadline passes, threads may still be alive and abandoned.
ProbeResult constructed with status 'timeout' and reason 'wall_clock' when box result is None; no check for other missing keys.
